article.title: Google Photos could soon let you take a shortcut straight to your favorite media
article.summary: TL;DR Google Photos version 7.90 includes an unreleased feature that could let you pin custom shortcuts to the Collections tab. In testing, long-pressing folders, albums, or people allowed pinning them to a horizontal scrolling bar at the top of the app. A dedicated Edit menu could let you reorder pinned items or browse organized library categories to customize your view. When Google replaced the classic Library view with the updated Collections tab, it promised a cleaner way to organize media. However, the top of the screen has remained largely rigid, with Google automatically and unilaterally deciding which shortcuts to highlight while burying your most-used folders. article.title: Orchestration is the new challenge for CX in the age of AI agents
article.summary: Presented by Tata Communications Enterprises are deploying AI agents, voice AI, and automation across messaging, voice, and digital channels faster than the architecture meant to support it. Most of that deployment has involved attaching conversational AI to legacy systems never built for it, says Gaurav Anand, global head of the Customer Interaction Suite at Tata Communications. "In the rush to deploy AI, organizations have largely bolted conversational AI onto legacy systems," Anand says. "As a result, while many enterprises have adopted digital tools, very few have platforms that are truly integrated, scaled, and capable of seamless orchestration." article.title: Ex-Googlers Are Planning AI-Human Hybrid to Prevent Rogue Models
article.summary: A new nonprofit founded by former Google researchers wants to keep humans at the center of AI development to ensure that the powerful technology is safe and less likely to escape its creators.
